text:
oliver: saw recurring latency spikes during tenant burst tests. autoscaler slams up then quickly drains, causing request failures. thinking we need explicit tokenized burst lanes + stronger hysteresis on scale-down. sketching proposal below.

tasha: strong +1. current soft-reservoirs are too local and amplify noisy bursts. token lanes per-tenant per-shard seems promising.

ben: can you summarise token model briefly? global vs local semantics?

oliver: idea: two-layer token model. each tenant has a global budget tracked in the ledger and each shard maintains a small local bucket seeded from global via periodic topups. Admission prefers local bucket (zero-RPC fastpath). On local miss, try a cheap CAS against the global ledger to borrow up to `borrow_cap`. Borrow is bounded and charged-back during reconciliation.

li: admission fastpath pseudo:
```
if local_bucket >= req: consume(local_bucket)
else if local_cache_global >= req and cas_reserve(global_key, delta): consume(global)
else deny
```
We keep `local_cache_global` with tiny TTL (50ms) to avoid thundering.

frank: CAS on ledger for every miss could be hot. suggest sharding ledger keys (tenant_id % N) and bulk topups to amortize.

oliver: agreed. also add an `optimistic_allowance_pct` (default 3%) where local admissions can temporarily overdraw the ledger without immediate CAS; reconciler later charges back. This keeps p99 low at cost of tiny transient overcommit.

tasha: important: make the optimistic path explicit in operator CRD so infra can opt-out on prod tenants: `burstPolicy.optimisticAllow` and `burstPolicy.optimisticPct`.

ben: autoscaler hysteresis: propose scale-up when queue_length > up_threshold for 20s, scale-down only if queue_length < down_threshold for 3m. plus `soft_drain_seconds` before node removal where we disable optimistic admits on that node to avoid losses during termination.

li: good. Also have a `preempt-reserve` flag for eviction: if node about to be reclaimed, we patrol and move ledger-backed reservations off it.

frank: metrics and alerts to add: `burst.local_tokens`, `burst.global_reserve`, `burst.optimistic_overdraw`, `autoscaler.scale_up_events`, `autoscaler.scale_down_events`, `reconciler.chargeback_failures`. Alert if `optimistic_overdraw` sustained > X or `chargeback_failures` spike.

oliver: migration/cutover plan: 1) ship metrics and local bucket only (no global borrow), 2) enable global ledger borrow read-only check (read consult only, still write local), 3) enable borrow writes + reconciler, 4) enable optimistic allowance. Each step behind feature-flags. During phase 2 we checkpoint local buckets to ledger with `bulk_checkpoint(pool_id, snapshot)` to prevent double-counting.

ben: rollback knobs: `admit.use_global_ledger=false`, `burst.optimisticAllow=false`, `admit.fallback=local|deny`. Add a K8s feature-flip in helm to toggle quickly.

tasha: ops runbook entries: page `dedicated-pool/burst-ops` with playbooks for `ledger-unavailable` (flip feature-flag to local-only), `chargeback-failures` (pause optimistic admits + run reconciler), and `checkpoint-conflicts` (retry window + force-rollback to local snapshot).

li: reliability concerns: need idempotent request IDs for claims and per-claim TTL so ledger entries auto-expire. reconciler should also expose `reclaimed_credits` rate.

frank: performance tests: synthetic with 5k tenants, random microbursts, measure admit latency p50/p95/p99 with optimisticAllow on/off. We want p50 under 4ms and p99 under 40ms.

ops-bot: scheduled: deploy `burst-controller` v0.3.0 to staging 2024-11-10T01:00Z by ops.

oliver: security: borrowing only within same tenant across shards. every borrow must be audited with request_id, caller pod, and shard.

ben: who owns what? tasha: operator/helm, oliver+li: runtime admits + reconciler, frank: perf harness + benchmarks, ben: RFC writeup and migration checklist.

li: I'll open dashboards PR and add alerts. please keep feature flags in the chart so we can toggle quickly during canaries.

oliver: thanks. i'll draft a short RFC summarizing decisions and include a simulation plan and exact rollback commands. :thumbsup:
